findings.title: Test cleanup registers removal of literal "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` (lines 381 and 425), using the literal string "alias" rather than the actual alias of the created provider ("idp-alias-" + i / "idp-alias-20"). As a result, none of the 21 identity providers created by the test are registered for cleanup, and cleanup instead issues DELETE requests for a non-existent "alias" provider (likely 404, which can fail the cleanup phase). The leaked providers include 10 IDPs that remain linked to organization "orga", so if testCacheIDPForLogin runs before testCacheIDPByOrg (JUnit method order is not guaranteed), testCacheIDPByOrg's assertion of exactly 6 IDPs for orga (orga-identity-provider + 5 linked) will fail. The same copy-paste bug exists at line 381 inside the creation loop and at line 425 for idp-alias-20 (and pre-exists at line 303 in testCacheIDPByOrg).

findings.title: remove() skips invalidating the internalId cache entry when the alias key is not cached
findings.body: In remove(alias), when the alias cache key is not in the session's invalidation set and there is no cached entry under the alias key, no invalidation is registered for the provider's internalId (the else-branch only calls registerIDPInvalidation when `cached != null`). An IDP can, however, be cached under its internalId via getById() without ever having been looked up by alias, so after remove() completes, a subsequent getById(internalId) can return the already-deleted identity provider from cache. This staleness matters even more now that getForLogin() and getByOrganization() resolve cached list entries through session.identityProviders().getById(id). The fix is to always invalidate the internalId (e.g. registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) in both branches, guarding for null). Note this hole pre-exists but the method was reworked in this PR and the new list caches depend on getById freshness.

findings.title: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate compares an org-aware wrapped original against the raw updated model
findings.body: In update(), the "original" model passed to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate comes from getById(), which returns the anonymous wrapper whose isEnabled() returns false whenever the linked organization is disabled (createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel). The "updated" model is the raw caller-supplied model whose isEnabled() is the stored value. The skip decisions in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate therefore depend on the organization's runtime enablement state rather than only on stored IDP attributes. Concrete scenario: an org-linked, public, enabled IDP whose organization is disabled appears in the cached getForLogin lists (the JPA query is config-based); if an admin then disables that IDP, both predicate tests evaluate to false and the login caches are NOT invalidated, leaving a disabled IDP in the cached getForLogin() stream. Correctness then relies entirely on every consumer re-checking isEnabled() — only the two OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean paths patched in this PR do so. Using the raw delegate model (idpDelegate.getById) as "original" would make the invalidation decision deterministic and independent of org state.
